assumptions: Memory structures are bounded by provider-level architecture.
Preference formation is a state-update process triggered by environmental inputs.
Information entropy can be modeled as variance in input data streams.
definition.falsification: If preference stability remains constant across both high-entropy and low-entropy input simulations, the hypothesis that architectural boundaries drive preference variance is falsified.
definition.statement: Architectural trust boundaries within WAKE systems constrain the accumulation of experiential memories, causing preference stability to correlate inversely with environmental information entropy.
definition.uncertainty: The degree to which WAKE provider boundaries actually isolate state remains theoretically grounded rather than empirically verified.

definition.method: Execute state transition simulation comparing high vs low entropy input streams.
definition.stop: Completion of 10 simulation runs per seed.
definition.success: Variance in stability between low and high entropy runs is statistically significant.

proposal.title: Advancing Can Memories Alone Shape Preferences? under enforced rotation

withheld_actions.task: Synthesize the role of architectural trust boundaries in constraining the experience-memory loop using results from the new entropy simulation.
